jobs.title: Data Scientist 6 - Experimentation Platform
jobs.excerpt: At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world.
jobs.description:
At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.

A culture of experimentation enables Netflix to continuously evolve and improve our products, delivering more joy to existing members and attracting new members from around the globe. Because experimentation is so pervasive at Netflix, we continually enable new capabilities and onboard new initiatives to the platform with close cross-functional collaboration with our Data Science partners.

At the nerve center of experimentation at Netflix is our internal, Netflix-wide Experimentation Platform (XP), responsible for all experiments across the company. We are looking for a Staff Data Scientist to help set the strategic direction for XP, elevate the rigor of causal inference across the company, and lead the consolidation of a decade of organically-grown, bespoke experimentation practices into a unified, modern platform - all with close cross-functional collaboration with our Data Science and Engineering partners.

This is a high-leverage role: rather than supporting a single team's experiments, you will set the standards, tooling, and product direction that every data scientist running an experiment at Netflix depends on.

Responsibilities

  • XP Strategy & Influence: Help set the strategy for the Experimentation Platform, including UI design, and user flows. Define how data scientists contribute metrics, reports, and templates to the platform so they have high leverage when setting standards for experiments in their own space.

  • Trust & Methodology: Verify that XP allocates, logs, and processes data using valid, trustworthy causal inference methods, and demonstrate that trustworthiness to partner teams - turning verification into automated, recurring, monitored practice rather than one-off checks.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Act as a strategic thought partner for data science and engineering stakeholders across Netflix. Bridge the gap between data science requirements and platform engineering implementation, representing the DS organization's needs directly to engineering leadership.

  • Platform Leadership: Influence and evolve how Netflix performs experimentation at scale - setting standards for inference practices (e.g. peeking, covariate adjustment, any-time valid methods, metric definitions, allocation mechanisms) and driving adoption of those practices across data science teams that range from long-tenured streaming teams to newer verticals like Ads.

  • Lead the consolidation of fragmented, bespoke experimentation systems into a coherent, maintainable platform by building the tools and processes that make best practice the path of least resistance.

  • Mentor and raise the bar for other team members working on or with the platform, and represent XP's point of view in company-wide discussions on experimentation methodology.

Qualifications

  • Advanced degree (PhD or Masters) in Computer Science, Statistics, Economics, Applied Mathematics, or a related quantitative field.

  • 8+ years of experience with statistics / causal inference in an experimentation context, including designing experiments at scale and diagnosing them when they break.

  • Demonstrated track record of setting standards or building tools that were adopted across multiple teams or an entire organization - not just applying judgment project by project.

  • Deep, practical knowledge of experimentation pitfalls and how to guard against them at a program level: sample ratio mismatches, winner's curse and regression to the mean, false discovery rate across a portfolio of tests, peeking, covariate adjustment, and allocation-vs-analysis-unit mismatches.

  • Experience translating ambiguous data science pain points into a sequenced product roadmap, including judgment on what a platform should build in, expose as a self-serve primitive, or explicitly not support.

  • 5+ years experience with data science languages, ideally including Python and SQL; comfort partnering closely with engineers on API/schema/system design.

  • Excellent cross-functional communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to influence skeptical stakeholders - both highly technical (data scientists, engineers) and non-technical business partners to adopt new methods or standards.

  • Curiosity to learn new statistics, methods, and optimization techniques, and the judgment to know when established methods are the better choice.

Since 2018, we’ve been pioneers in payment orchestration, enabling enterprise brands to optimise their infrastructure and create frictionless digital experiences. From travel giants to household retail names, our global customer base is growing fast, supported by world-class partners like Visa and Worldpay.

The journey so far has been incredible, but we’re just getting started. We are looking for exceptional talent to join us as we continue to grow.

We are seeking a Senior Partnership Manager to take ownership of a portfolio of strategic payment partnerships. You will play a pivotal role in turning high-value industry relationships into tangible commercial growth, stronger customer propositions, and long-term business value. Your day-to-day will include:

This role is for a Senior Partnership Manager who wants to turn complex payment relationships into clear commercial outcomes. We are looking for someone who balances commercial drive with strategic rigour and cross-functional leadership.

  • Strong cross-functional alignment skills, with experience coordinating complex initiatives across commercial, product, and technical teams.

Nice to Have

  • Experience supporting merchants operating in complex, regulated, or high-volume industries.

  • Growth: A culture that champions career progression and gives you the autonomy to directly contribute to an innovative tech business as it scales.
  • Community: Quarterly in-person team events and monthly socials to keep our remote team connected.

Ready to bridge the gap? Apply to be a BR-DGE Builder today.

jobs.excerpt: iFIT’s vision is to create the world's most holistic health and fitness platform, integrating all elements of health - physical fitness, mental health, nutrition and active recovery - into a seamless interactive experience.
jobs.description:
iFIT’s vision is to create the world's most holistic health and fitness platform, integrating all elements of health - physical fitness, mental health, nutrition and active recovery - into a seamless interactive experience. We develop proprietary software that learns and adjusts to the habits of each person as it delivers immersive content that guides them on their own individual fitness journey.

iFIT is creating a new Director, Enterprise AI Enablement role to lead the company's shift toward AI-powered ways of working. This is a high-visibility, high-impact role that sits at the intersection of technology, enablement, and enterprise strategy.

Reporting to the VP of Information Technology, you will shape iFIT's strategy for AI tooling and governance, co-chairing the established cross-functional AI Governance Committee and setting the guardrails that keep AI use responsible and compliant. You will also help set the technical standards and patterns business teams build on, so AI use cases across the company are consistent and able to scale.

With those guardrails and patterns in place, the heart of the role is transforming how iFIT runs, from manual, human-driven workflows to intelligent, AI-powered operations. You will lead a community of business AI leaders across the operational functions, training, coaching, and equipping them to put AI to work in their own areas. As a force multiplier, your job is to lift the whole company, helping teams build and sustain this work on their own and keep improving as they grow more capable. This mission keeps you hands-on. As a player/coach, you will work with each function to find automation opportunities and build alongside teams to speed results. That proximity keeps you close to the business, strengthening relationships and your grasp of how the work really flows, so you always know what will help most and where iFIT should invest next.

This role is ideal for a proven AI and automation leader who pairs technical depth with business fluency, able to spot where automation will pay off across the business, and build it, while raising AI capability across the whole company.

COMMITMENTS

  • Stand up the community of business AI leaders across the priority functions, with the roster, cadence, and working relationships to drive adoption and automation from within each team.
  • Establish the foundation for responsible AI: the guardrails, technical standards, and the framework for evaluating and monitoring agents so they can be trusted in production.
  • Identify the highest-value automation opportunities across the business and deliver early, tangible wins, including automating business processes that span multiple areas of the company.
  • Build the operating rhythm that sustains momentum: a working feedback loop, adoption and impact metrics, and a prioritized roadmap leadership can act on.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Set Strategy, Standards & Governance

  • Shape iFIT's strategy for AI tooling and governance, deciding which platforms and tools the company standardizes on and where to focus first for the biggest operational gain.
  • Help set the technical standards, architecture, and patterns business teams build on, so AI use across the company is consistent, sound, and able to scale.
  • Monitor the fast-moving AI market and continually assess emerging tools and techniques, so iFIT invests early in what will matter and keeps its edge.
  • Co-chair the cross-functional AI Governance Committee, alongside a Legal and an IT infrastructure lead, setting the guardrails and approved-tool standards that keep AI use responsible and compliant.

Activate AI Across the Business

  • Build and lead a community of business AI leaders across the operational functions, Finance, HR, Supply Chain, Marketing, Product, and beyond, coaching and equipping them to put AI to work inside their own areas.
  • Make sure every function gets the training it needs to use AI well, whether you deliver it directly, bring in outside expertise, or equip teams with materials they can share themselves.
  • Enable these teams to build and sustain AI-powered work within and across their own functions, growing what the whole company can do.
  • Help teams redesign how the work actually gets done around AI, moving from manual, human-driven workflows to AI-powered ways of working.
  • Spread what works from one team to the next, turning wins in one function into repeatable practice across the company.

Build Hands-On as a Player/Coach

  • Work closely with teams to understand how their work flows, and advise on where AI and automation can help, whether or not you are the one who builds it.
  • Roll up your sleeves and build alongside teams, taking a defined need and delivering the tools, automations, or templates to meet it, then handing them off for the teams to own and run.
  • Integrate AI agents and automations into existing enterprise systems (ERP, CRM, HRIS, and the like), working alongside IT Engineering to keep solutions sound and stable.
  • Keep improving what is already live: harden the automations teams depend on and refine them as needs change.

Measure and Improve

  • Track the impact of AI across the business, from efficiency and error reduction to adoption and output by team, and report it to the VP, IT and executive leadership.
  • Monitor the agents and automations deployed across the company, tracking performance and output quality, watching for behavior that goes off track, and ensuring responsible use and data security.
  • Turn what you learn working alongside the business into program improvements, refining the tools, training, and guardrails, and flagging the new AI capabilities iFIT should invest in or pursue next.

QUALIFICATIONS

Required

  • You are an experienced, AI-forward software engineer with 6+ years in a senior or lead capacity.
  • You have delivered products, integrations, and automations that produced measurable business benefits. You build sustainably, documenting how things work and training others to run and maintain them, so what you hand off keeps working without you.
  • Strong working fluency with agentic AI systems: you understand how agent loops, tool use, RAG, and multi-agent workflows fit together, and you can build and integrate them with enterprise data and systems.
  • You understand why evaluating an agent for accuracy, reliability, and safety matters, and you can use evaluation tooling to confirm an agent is sound before it goes live.
  • You have worked as a technical developer directly alongside business teams, giving you real business fluency: you can map how a function works, translate between the technical and business sides, and bring the acumen to earn credibility and steer toward the right outcomes.
  • A track record as a force multiplier: leading a community of practitioners, coaching and training people to adopt new tools and ways of working, and raising the capability of an entire organization rather than delivering all the work yourself.

Preferred

  • Deeper hands-on engineering with agentic systems: designing multi-agent orchestration and self-correction, standing up or extending evaluation and test harnesses, and applying standards like MCP and human-in-the-loop controls in production.
  • Prior experience on an AI or technology governance body, helpful, though not required given the co-chair nature of the role.
  • Experience in a consumer products, health & fitness, or direct-to-consumer e-commerce environment.
  • Familiarity with enterprise platforms such as SAP, Salesforce, or Workday, and experience layering AI agents onto them.
  • You have created structured training or curriculum materials that people used to onboard themselves without your direct involvement.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

In the First 90 Days

  • AI Governance Committee co-chair role assumed, with guardrails and approved-tool standards drafted for review.
  • Community of business AI leaders established, with named leaders across the priority functions and a regular meeting cadence in place.
  • Business impact metrics and a prioritized opportunity roadmap defined and shared with leadership.
  • Framework for measuring and monitoring production AI, covering performance, quality, responsible behavior, and data security, drafted for executive review.
  • At least one hands-on win delivered, a tool, automation, or template in active use and removing a real bottleneck.

By Year One

  • Team leaders operating independently, standing up AI-driven workflows in their own business areas without support.
  • Community of business AI leaders active and self-sustaining, carrying good practice from one function to the next on its own momentum.

We take care of our people. Parnall Law has been recognized as one of Albuquerque's best places to work year after year — and that's no accident. Here's what you can look forward to:

  • Desire to learn, develop, and motivate team members

What You'll Do

As a Billing Specialist at Parnall Law, you are a critical advocate for our clients behind the scenes — ensuring every provider bill is submitted correctly, every insurance carrier pays on time, and every client walks away with the maximum possible recovery.

MISSION STATEMENT

The mission of the Billing Specialist is to ensure all providers submit their bills to health insurance or automobile (MedPay) insurance in a timely manner and further ensures the proper insurance carriers pay the provider bills in a timely manner, maximizing the net recovery for the client. Further, the Billing Specialist will verify all provider balances in a timely manner so that the settlement funds can be distributed to the client as soon as settlement funds are received.

Making justice count, down to the last cent.

RESULTS / OUTCOMES(What you must get done.)

  • Attend firm-wide huddle every Monday at 8:00 AM
  • Attend daily team mini huddles Tuesday through Friday at 8:00 AM

  • Open all subrogation claims within 14 days of the signed retainer
  • Submit Med Pay and Health Insurance information to all treating providers within 30 days of being retained
  • Submit Med Pay and Health Insurance information to all treating providers when providers are updated by Case Manager, within 15 days of new provider information
  • Request final health insurance and Med Pay ledgers within 7 days of the client finishing treatment and being moved to Prep
  • Verify all required outstanding medical balances within 7 days when a case moves into negotiations
  • Verify any outstanding medical balances within 5 days of a case being settled
  • Maintain a biweekly activity level of 1,000 or more in SmartAdvocate
  • Ensure overdue tasks never exceed 60

DUTIES / RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Follow up with all providers after providing Med Pay and health insurance information to ensure bills are being properly submitted to the proper carrier
  • Maintain accurate records of all bills, payments, adjustments, and remaining balances to facilitate negotiating discounts by disbursement staff, paralegals, and attorneys — maximizing recovery for our clients
  • Coordinate benefits with available insurance including but not limited to Med Pay, health insurance, Medicaid, Medicare, Veterans Benefits, and other federal and state programs
  • Open claims and submit necessary documents for Medicare and Tricare benefits
  • Maintain the client's Medicare portal
  • Answer incoming calls via the First Call Group
  • Monitor dashboard metrics/KPIs and actively work to keep those metrics in top shape
  • Follow and maintain all firm policies and procedures

REPORTING RELATIONSHIP

  • Reports directly to Settlement Department Team Lead

  3. Energy (“Vibes”). You’re the main point of contact for clients and internal teams. You bring clarity, positivity, and momentum. When things get busy or complicated, you keep people focused and motivated.

Skills, Knowledge and Traits

You do not need prior A/B testing experience or even formal project management experience. We will train you. Here’s what we need from you:
  1. Organization and diligence. You like systems, checklists, and timelines. You front-load work, plan ahead, and don’t stop until things are finished properly.

  3. Smart and high agency. You learn quickly, enjoy technology and design, and want to understand why things work (or don’t). You’re the kind of person who notices patterns and asks good questions.

jobs.title: Senior IT Engineer
jobs.excerpt: The role You are where things stop being stuck.  When our Senior Support Analysts cannot resolve something, it comes to you — and when you cannot resolve it, the question is no longer "who troubleshoots better," it is "what should the standard be.
jobs.description:
The role

You are where things stop being stuck.

When our Senior Support Analysts cannot resolve something, it comes to you — and when you cannot resolve it, the question is no longer "who troubleshoots better," it is "what should the standard be." That is a design question for our Architect. Everything short of it is yours.

You are also the person who keeps our customer environments operable and conformant to standard: correcting drift, executing the complex changes, and — importantly — holding the authority to stop something that would leave the team supporting a mess.

That halt authority is real here. If you can see that a deliverable will generate six months of support pain, we want you to say so and stop it.

What you will do

Keeping things running

  • Act as the terminal operational escalation point for the Services team
  • Take technical command during major incidents: direct diagnosis, decide actions, keep leadership informed
  • Execute complex change beyond established standards, safely, with rollback planned
  • Remediate environments back to standard and keep them there
  • Run post-incident reviews that actually change something — a standard, a runbook, an automation
  • Develop our Tier 2 analysts deliberately, not incidentally

Delivering change

(roughly 40–50% of your time, with a dedicated Implementation Engineer seat planned as this work grows)

  • Lead migrations, server and cloud transitions, and new customer onboardings
  • Implement our Workplace OS layers to defined standard
  • Validate that what gets built can be operated by the team, and hand it over properly

What you bring

Experience

  • Five or more years supporting and engineering Microsoft environments, with real time in a managed services or multi-customer setting
  • A track record of owning complex problems end to end, and of executing change in production without incident

Technical depth

  • Microsoft 365 in depth: Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint, Intune, Defender, Purview fundamentals
  • Entra ID and Active Directory in depth — hybrid identity, authentication flows, Conditional Access
  • Windows Server: AD, Group Policy, DNS, DHCP, file services, certificates
  • Azure infrastructure: virtual machines, networking, storage, backup, Site Recovery, governance and cost
  • Security in practice: MFA, Conditional Access, endpoint protection, patch and vulnerability management, Zero Trust, CIS familiarity
  • Networking to a genuine troubleshooting standard. Cisco Meraki and Barracuda are directly relevant.
  • PowerShell for administration and automation
  • Backup, continuity, and DR — designing it and proving it works
  • Valued certifications: Microsoft endpoint and administrator paths, the SC series, AZ-104 / AZ-305 / AZ-500

How you work

  • Diagnostic rigour under pressure. Staying systematic when a customer is down and everyone is watching.
  • Design judgement with standards deference. You know what good looks like and you still choose the standard over your own preference. That combination is rarer than raw skill and matters more to us.
  • Risk calibration. Blast radius, rollback, and the discipline to stop.
  • Teaching by default. You leave the team more capable than you found it.
  • Plain-language translation. Explaining technical reality without condescension and without false comfort.
  • Interest in automation. You do not have to be a developer. You do have to notice repetition and want it gone.

Why this role, here, now

We are honest about our situation: this seat is currently open, and its absence is being felt. That means two things for you. The work is needed and you will see your impact immediately. And you are joining a team that has just redesigned how it operates specifically so that this role is not the impossible everything-seat it can become elsewhere — escalation and project delivery are explicitly bounded, and a dedicated implementation seat is planned as that work grows.

Where it goes

Three capability bands within the tier, with compensation attached. From here: Architect, via standards and design contribution; Implementation Engineer, if delivery is your preference; or depth in seat, which is a legitimate and well-compensated answer. You will have a development plan, technical direction from our Architect, and protected time to grow.

What we offer

  • Salary range: $80,000 – $99,000
  • Personally tailored benefits - health, vision, dental, and paramedical
  • Flexibility in how, when, and where you work across a 4.5-day workweek, with a vacation policy well above standard
  • Focus windows that protect deep, uninterrupted work
  • Broad exposure to technology through client engagements and lab environments
  • Funded lifelong learning: an immersive education platform, vendor training, and soft-skills development
  • Wellness support, including access to the employee wellness platform and a wellness allowance
  • A defined career framework with development plans, capability bands, and protected development time
  • An open voice in shaping the direction of the company, with leadership that serves your best interest
  • Work. Life. Balance.

About Third Octet

We are a Canadian managed IT services provider, working since 2007 with small and mid-sized businesses — typically 25 to 150 employees — across the Greater Toronto Area and beyond. Our Workplace Suite is built on Microsoft 365, Microsoft Azure, Cisco Meraki, Barracuda, and Lenovo, and we are expanding it into Workplace OS: a deliberate operating model that layers shared visibility, governed automation, insights, and AI onto a secure, standardized foundation.

We are a small team supporting a growing base of customers, which means the work is real, the ownership is genuine, and what you build actually gets used.

How we screen

We use automated tools to help sort and shortlist applications. Every candidate who reaches the shortlist is reviewed by a person before any decision is made.

The Business Intelligence Analyst plays a key role in supporting data-informed decisions across eMoney by transforming raw data into meaningful insights. This role goes beyond foundational analysis by independently managing analytics projects, developing dashboards, implementing business logic, and partnering closely with business units to solve complex problems. The Business Intelligence Analyst defines KPIs, contributes to data governance, and ensures data integrity across systems.   • Analyze and interpret structured and unstructured data from multiple sources to uncover trends, patterns, and opportunities.
  • Design and develop reports and dashboards using BI tools (e.g., Power BI, Looker), aligning outputs with stakeholder needs and business goals.
  • Translate business logic into technical specifications and implement calculations, KPIs, and rules in analytics environments.
  • Conduct exploratory analysis and hypothesis testing to validate assumptions and guide business decisions.
  • Collaborate with data engineers and developers to ensure data flows, structures, and integrations meet analytical requirements.
  • Contribute to data governance efforts by creating, maintaining, and enforcing data definitions, metadata, and lineage documentation.
  • Apply data quality and validation techniques to improve trust in data across the organization.
  • Partner with operational and cross-functional teams to identify opportunities to optimize processes, improve client experience, and increase revenue.
  • Utilize basic data modeling techniques (e.g., star/snowflake schema) and assist in the development of data pipelines and ETL workflows.
  • Present findings to diverse audiences, using visual storytelling and plain-language explanations to drive alignment and action.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in a quantitative discipline – math, statistics, data and analytics preferred or equivalent experience
  • 3+ years’ experience in data science, statistical analysis, business intelligence or related consultative role

Skills

  • Working knowledge of data modeling concepts (e.g., star schema, snowflake, normalization).
  • Familiarity with data pipeline/ETL processes and collaboration with data engineering teams.
  • Hands-on experience with data visualization and reporting tools (e.g., Power BI, Looker, Tableau).
  • Exposure to Python or other scripting languages for analysis or automation is a plus.
  • Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving abilities, with attention to detail and data accuracy.
  • Ability to clearly communicate findings and translate technical insights into business recommendations for both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Experience contributing to data governance, including data quality practices, definitions, and metadata maintenance.
  • Comfortable managing priorities and working independently within fast-paced, collaborative environments.
  • Strong attention to detail

The Payroll Manager operates at the intersection of Finance, HR, and Compliance — partnering cross-functionally to align payroll practices with organizational goals and regulatory requirements.

Location: Remote, candidates based in Central and Eastern time zones preferred; candidates located elsewhere will also be considered

Core Responsibilities & Expectations for the Role

  • Own and execute full-cycle payroll processing for all employee types (salaried, hourly, contractors) using the company’s payroll module, ensuring on-time and accurate disbursements, reviewing and reconciling pre-payroll reports before each run, and investigating/resolving discrepancies prior to submission
  • Process off-cycle payrolls, manual checks, and retroactive adjustments as needed
  • Manage final pay calculations for terminated employees in compliance with applicable state law timelines
  • Serve as the first point of contact for employee payroll inquiries — resolving issues related to pay stubs, direct deposit, tax withholding, corrections, and guiding employees through self-service payroll system features (pay stub access, W-4 updates, direct deposit setup)
  • Manage tax filings and remittances, including quarterly 941s, annual W-2s, 1099s, and any state/local equivalents.
  • Configure automated payroll workflows and approval chains to minimize manual intervention and reduce error risk.
  • Participate in HR and Finance system projects, including implementations, upgrades, and cross-functional initiatives.
  • Document all payroll processes, procedures, and internal controls to support consistency and business continuity.
  • Coordinate with the HR/Benefits team to ensure accurate and timely payroll deductions for medical, dental, vision, 401(k), HSA/FSA, and other voluntary benefits
  • Provide payroll data to support budgeting, forecasting, accounting, and financial planning activities.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Human Resources, or related field
  • 2-5 years of progressive payroll management experience
  • Experience processing payroll for 200+ employees across multiple states, including required experience with California and Illinois payroll
  • Prior experience in a standalone or lead payroll role preferred
  • Minimum 2 years of direct, hands-on experience administering payroll in Rippling (or similar small workforce management platform), including system configuration, pay group management, tax settings, and workflow automation
  • Experience with additional platforms (ADP, Paylocity, Workday, etc.) is a plus including payroll system implementation, transition, and system training for employees
  • Advanced skills for payroll reconciliation, VLOOKUP/pivot tables, and data analysis
  • Understanding of how Rippling connects with benefits carriers, time & attendance systems, and GL platforms
  • CPP (Certified Payroll Professional) designation preferred; FPC (Fundamental Payroll Certification) considered

jobs.description:
Job Title: Director of the Beyond Coal Campaign
Department: Program - Campaigns
Location: Remote
Reports to: Senior Director for Campaign Strategy
Supervises: Up to 6 campaign staff
Context: At the Sierra Club, we believe in the power of interdependence. Together, we remain committed to the fight for a healthy climate built on a foundation of environmental, racial, economic, and gender justice – a future where all people benefit from a healthy, thriving planet and a direct connection to nature. As the climate crisis and deeply entrenched systemic racism all fuel injustice, we will continue to fight for a bold, transformational agenda that recognizes the interconnectedness between our planet, our humanity, and our future. By recognizing that our destinies are tied, we continue to name that all things are fundamentally connected, and the overlap between ecology, race, gender, and representative government will move to either advance our collective humanity or to oppress it. Sierra Club has close to 800 staff across the country and a network of 64 local chapters that are led and fueled by thousands of volunteers. We are also proud to be a unionized employer, with three labor unions representing more than half of our employees.
Scope: The Director of the Beyond Coal Campaign leads the Sierra Club’s work to achieve an equitable transformation of the power sector away from coal and gas to 100 percent clean energy. This is a senior leadership position within the Sierra Club. The Director of the Beyond Coal Campaign serves as the campaign’s lead fundraiser and the primary relationship manager for the foundations and major donors who invest in this work, and is accountable for translating that investment into clear strategy, measurable results, and meaningful outcomes for both communities and donors.
The Director of the Beyond Coal Campaign sets high-level power sector strategy, approves local campaign plans, and raises and deploys resources to achieve the organization’s top goals The Director of the Beyond Coal Campaign will foster collaboration with Beyond Coal staff as well as teams across other Sierra Club Energy Campaigns and will be capable of managing internal and external opportunities and challenges. The Campaign Director will do all of the above in a way that ensures strategies and tactics leverage opportunities to advance justice (centered on racial justice), equity, and inclusion while building long-term power.

Job activities include but are not limited to:

    1. Lead fundraising for the Beyond Coal Campaign. Serve as the campaign’s principal fundraiser, responsible for securing the revenue that powers the campaign’s annual budget. Build and manage a pipeline of institutional and individual funding prospects; cultivate, solicit, and close six- and seven-figure grants and gifts from foundations and high-net-worth individuals; and partner closely with the Office of Advancement on prospect strategy, proposal development, presentations, and reporting. Set annual revenue goals, own performance against them, and adjust campaign expenses based on quarterly revenue projections and strategic opportunity.
    1. Steward the campaign’s donor relationships. Serve as the primary programmatic contact for the campaign’s foundation and major-donor partners. Maintain a proactive cadence of updates, briefings, and meetings; lead the drafting of grant deliverables and reports, and ensure they are completed on time and at high quality; communicate campaign impact and return on investment in terms that matter to each funder; and manage funder expectations through moments of change. Ensure knowledge of each relationship is documented so that it belongs to the institution, not only to individuals.
    1. Manage a large, complex budget. Ensure we are providing donors a meaningful return on investment, achieving our stated goals, and aligning resources with strategy on an ongoing basis. Owns strategy and budgetary decisions, deploying resources in service of Beyond Coal Campaign and power sector goals through a consultative and collaborative approach.
    1. Lead campaign strategy, planning, design, and evaluation for the Beyond Coal Campaign, centered in equity, justice, and inclusion, that meets the challenge of the current climate crisis. Develop an actionable theory of change, core strategies, and campaign goals and outcomes. Continue to build and elevate the campaign and organization’s work to accelerate the buildout of clean energy, retire existing coal plants, and block new gas plants. Engage across the organization and the movement to ensure the campaign is rooted in equitable outcomes and contributes to building long-term power. Oversee strategic campaign planning at the national level, and support local planning. Approves local plans in partnership with relevant stakeholders.
    1. Provide strategic leadership to the Sierra Club and those implementing the Beyond Coal Campaign strategy. The Director will need to effectively delegate, follow-up, and project manage in a rapidly changing environment with competing demands. Serve as the strategic lead and provide guidance to all parts of the Sierra Club and with partners and external stakeholders related to the Beyond Coal Campaign. Accountable for building strong relationships across groups of stakeholders to ensure goal alignment, support for staff engaged in the Beyond Coal Campaign work, and compelling narratives to advance outcomes. Lead the Beyond Coal Campaign team’s engagement with the Field Department and Chapters, Environmental Law Program, Communications, and deputize staff and delegates work as appropriate.
    1. Supervise and mentor up to 6 direct reports by setting performance objectives, providing regular feedback, and supporting staff to excel. Effectively manage, guide, and coach staff; ensure individual professional development; establish performance objectives and expectations; and evaluate accomplishments and effectiveness. Take appropriate disciplinary action when needed, and make hiring and termination recommendations. Ensure campaign staff advance assigned projects by collaborating with other Sierra Club staff and volunteers as well as external partners. Establish strategic priorities and monitor progress toward annual results.
    1. Serve as a member of the Energy Campaigns Team. Help shape and manage the direction of intersectional energy campaigns, and support a holistic vision for significant greenhouse gas reductions across interrelated sectors of the economy. Support an effective and visionary theory of change for the Energy Campaigns that leverages the power of the campaigns as part of the Sierra Club’s foundational approach to greenhouse gas and harmful pollution reductions while also building power.
    1. Serve as a spokesperson. Represent the Sierra Club with the media and with partners as a strategic leader and subject-matter expert on issues related to the campaign.
    2. Perform miscellaneous duties as directed.

The successful candidate must demonstrate the following skills, experience and competencies:

    • Successful track record of fundraising and donor stewardship. Demonstrated success personally raising significant revenue—including six- and seven-figure grants and gifts—from foundations and high-net-worth individuals, spanning cultivation, solicitation, closing, reporting, and renewal. Experience partnering with advancement or development staff on proposals, presentations, and donor communications. Experience writing successful grant proposals and grant reports, and a record of retaining and growing funder relationships over time, including through moments of organizational or leadership change.
      • Track record of successful organizational leadership or campaign leadership. Demonstrated ability to build, implement, and win strategic campaigns or build successful organizations. Demonstrated ability to set a vision and achieve goals in an operating environment that requires working with and building alignment among a range of stakeholders inside and outside the organization. Includes identifying a theory of change, leveraging resources both internal and external toward strategies designed to win tangible, meaningful outcomes, and building a team culture that supports success.
        • Effective executive leadership and project management ability. This is a high profile, fast-paced position with many competing priorities and demands. Successful candidates will have extensive experience managing and leading projects from end-to-end, establishing and implementing relevant coordination processes, delegating effectively, and leading a large team. Strong interpersonal skills to navigate disagreement and lead through uncertainty, ambiguity, or conflict.
          • Knowledge related to the power sector and related environmental and social justice issues that arise in that work. Experience in policy and other important regulatory and related frameworks governing the power sector.
            • Understanding of environmental, climate, and social justice issues and how they relate to each other. Demonstrated ability to design and implement strategies that operate at the intersections of the environment and race, gender, and class. Experience cultivating and maintaining just, accountable partnerships, especially with organizations led by those most impacted by the crises we seek to remedy.
              • Skillful at managing individuals and leading teams with a diversity of identities and skill sets to contribute at their highest level. Proficient at proactively surfacing and navigating conflict in a generative, equitable way, and providing timely feedback. In-depth understanding of privilege and how race, gender, and class intersect with environmental, climate, and movement work. Personal commitment to learning and growth, especially around equity, and experience coaching others on these issues.
                • Highly developed communication skills, and the ability to represent the organization in media and in venues with key decision-makers (including elected officials at all levels, their senior staffers, movement leaders and tribal partners, and C-suite executives).
                  • Successful track record of budget management at comparable scale, aligning resources with strategy and demonstrating a meaningful return on investment to donors.
                    • Committed to evolution. You are committed to continuously deepening and evolving your own understanding of systems of oppression through study, openness, and humility. And you easily recognize your own relationship to privilege and power, examining and shifting your behaviors as appropriate.
                      • Uplifting and additive. You see mistakes as opportunities for growth, problems as catalysts for solutions, and inspire others along the journey. You carry a constructive approach, can-do attitude, a sense of humor, and authentic kindness wherever you go.
                        • Ability to travel up to 25% of the time.

Strongest candidates will demonstrate the following skills, experience and competencies:

    • Existing relationships with climate, clean energy, and environmental funders, and experience stewarding institutional grants and major gifts of significant scale.
      • Proven ability to integrate cutting-edge data management and digital tools to inform strategy and track progress.
        • Demonstrated experience in implementing change management processes that required building buy-in and leading across a wide range of stakeholders.
          • Experience working in a fast-paced environment, across geographies, and with different types of volunteer and staff structures, exercising effective judgment in challenging situations and remaining calm under pressure.

To Apply

The Sierra Club provides equal employment and advancement opportunities to all staff members. Employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, lived experience and skills. The Sierra Club does not discriminate in employment opportunities or practices on the basis of race, color, creed, religion, national origin, immigration status, socioeconomic status, ancestry, age, size, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, familial status, veteran status, disability, AIDS/HIV status, medical condition, prior conviction, arrest history, traits historically associated with race, including, but not limited to, hair texture and protective hairstyles, or any other characteristic protected by law.

The Sierra Club values applicants who are people that identify as Black, Indigenous, and other minoritized groups; women; queer, transgender, gender non-conforming, and gender fluid people.

Explore, enjoy and protect the planet.

What We Offer

Working at Twilio offers many benefits, including competitive pay, generous time off, ample parental and wellness leave, healthcare, a retirement savings program, and much more. Offerings vary by location.

The successful candidate’s starting salary will be determined based on permissible, non-discriminatory factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location.

Additionally, we empower employees to build positive change in their communities by supporting their volunteering and donation efforts.

We will never ask for payment, gift cards, cryptocurrency, or banking information during the recruiting process. jobs.description:
Care Coordinator

About FamilyWell Health

FamilyWell Health is an AI-enabled mental health startup dedicated to addressing the women's mental health crisis by seamlessly embedding high-quality, equitable, and affordable mental health care into women’s health practices and health systems. Our comprehensive virtual care model delivers evidence-based mental health services across the full reproductive lifecycle, from fertility through menopause, using the proven Collaborative Care Model (CoCM).

Our platform integrates coaching, therapy, psychiatry, and care coordination services directly into clinical workflows, making mental health care accessible, affordable, and insurance-covered. With 95% of patients experiencing clinical improvement within four months, FamilyWell is addressing one of healthcare's most underserved areas while building a financially sustainable model for provider partners.

Following our recent Series A raise, we are expanding nationally and seeking exceptional leaders to join our mission-driven team. Learn more at .

Role:

The Care Coordinator (CC) is a non-clinical member of FamilyWell’s care team and plays a pivotal role in supporting patients throughout their reproductive journey. CCs also provide program management and logistical support for FamilyWell’s partnering women’s health clinic. This role focuses on care coordination, engagement, and navigation. CCs do not provide therapy, clinical assessment, diagnosis, or medical advice.

CCs guide patients through every step of FamilyWell’s integrated mental health program, working closely with a cross-disciplinary team to ensure seamless communication, timely follow-up, and a consistently positive patient experience. They support patients across a wide range of acuity levels by providing compassionate outreach, coordinating referrals, monitoring progress, and helping patients stay engaged in care throughout their FamilyWell journey.

Reports To: Lead Care Coordinator

Compensation: W2 Hourly role compensated at $25/hr, may be eligible for benefits depending on number of hours hours/week

Location: Remote

Start Date: Immediate

Key Responsibilities:

Patient Engagement:

  • Communicate with patients through various channels (text, phone) to facilitate program engagement, provide reminders, and follow up on care.
  • Maintain strong engagement and satisfaction among patients through ongoing support and education

Care Coordination and Documentation:

  • Update patient records in Electronic Health Records (EHRs) and communicate care plans to referring clinic partners.
  • Maintain a collaborative care registry to track patient follow-up and clinical outcomes.
  • Prepare and submit routine progress reports in the EHR.
  • Facilitate outside referrals for community-based social services as clinically indicated (e.g., housing assistance, vocational rehabilitation, mental health specialty care, substance abuse treatment).
  • Care Coordinators do not handle crisis stabilization independently; they escalate to licensed clinical team members per protocol.

Reporting and Collaboration:

  • Compose, prepare, and communicate timely patient and provider responses to questions.
  • Report directly to the Lead Care Coordinator and provide regular updates on patient engagement and clinical outcomes.
  • Collaborate with OB clinic staff to ensure coordinated care and support for patients.

Qualifications

Education:

  • Required: Bachelor’s degree and/or Master’s Degree in nursing, social work or psychology
  • Clinical licensure not required for this role

Skills:

  • Strong understanding of women’s mental health conditions, treatments, and community resources.
  • Excellent communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Comfortability with managing a high volume caseload of patients across varying acuity levels.
  • Ability to engage and educate patients in a compassionate and supportive manner.
  • Strong ability to collaborate across departments including Care Operations and Partner Success
  • Proficiency in using EHR systems and maintaining accurate patient records.
  • Proficiency in using Google Suite.

Key Competencies:

  • Empathy and Compassion: Ability to understand and support the unique challenges of pregnant/ postpartum patients and patients experiencing menopause.
  • Engagement Skills: Proficient in maintaining patient engagement and satisfaction with the program.
  • Communication: Strong verbal and written communication skills for effective patient and provider interactions.
  • Organizational Skills: Ability to manage patient records, track outcomes, and ensure timely follow-up.
  • Cultural Sensitivity: Respectful of diverse backgrounds and experiences, particularly in a perinatal and menopause context.
  • Adaptability: We’re a fast growing company, constantly looking to make improvements as we go. Our team is smart, resilient, and always iterating to make our program even better for our patients.

Please be aware of recruitment scams. FamilyWell will never ask candidates to pay money, request sensitive personal information early in the process, or conduct interviews over unsecured platforms. All official communication will come from an @ email address.

Notre client souhaite intégrer un(e) spécialiste QA capable de planifier, coordonner et exécuter les activités de tests dans le cadre de projets de transformation, d’évolution de systèmes et d’optimisation de processus. At DUAL North America, our core values dictate how we live and work. We are a group with independence and people at its heart and we are a home for talent with a unique culture: the biggest small company in the world.

The focus on being a People First business has always been at the very heart of the Group; Our vision was to create an independent business with a unique culture and one that would survive and thrive as a business controlled by the people working for it. And finding the most talented and entrepreneurial people to join the Group has been and will continue to be key.

DUAL North America, Inc. is seeking a

Sr. Casualty Examiner Construction

  • Sr. Casualty Examiner, Construction

  • Classification: Exempt/Full-time

  • Reports to: Claims Manager

  • Travel: 0-10%

  • Salary/hourly: $125,000.00-$145,000.00

  • Location: Remote

Role overview

DUAL North America is seeking a Senior Casualty Examiner for the Construction Defect Claims team.

At DUAL, Sr. Casualty Examiners play a critical role in managing moderate to high exposure claims with accuracy and efficiency, while complying with state regulatory requirements. In this role, you will investigate claims, analyze policy coverages, and collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to ensure claim resolution.

Supporting the Construct Defect Claims team, you will independently manage moderate to high exposure claims involving alleged defects in residential and commercial construction.

Role responsibilities

• Make initial contacts with interest parties

• Handle moderate to high exposure construction defect claims involving residential and commercial projects.

• Analyze coverage and draft coverage position letters as needed

• Conduct liability investigations

• Comply with DOI regulations

• Retain and coordinate with defense counsel and experts to develop and execute agreed-upon litigation strategies, while managing plans and budgets to ensure effective case resolution

• Coordinate the retention of experts, subject to an agreed upon budget

• Establish timely indemnity and expense reserves based on an exposure analysis that is documented in the claim file, revisiting reserve adequacy on a continual basis

• Draft well written and comprehensive captioned reports to request reserve and settlement authority on higher exposure cases that outline all critical aspects of the case in preparation for roundtable presentations to the carrier partners

• Travel up to 10% to attend mediations, settlements conferences and trials on appropriate cases

• Keep current on key changes in case law and industry trends

• Assist underwriting and other business partners

Key requirements

• Bachelor’s degree preferred

• Professional designations (CPCU, SCLA, AIC, JD) are a plus

• 7+ years of construction defect claims experience is required with consistent high level of performance and achievement

• Must be licensed or have the ability to become licensed in all required states

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint

• Advanced knowledge of end-to-end claims handling, including litigation

• Knowledge of industry trends and legal developments affecting claims handling

• Ability to manage multiple claims and competing priorities

• Ability to adapt to evolving regulatory and legal environments

• Complete assigned tasks correctly, on time and able to learn quickly

• Self-motivated and demonstrating attention to detail

• Be able to work independently for extended periods

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills as well as general business understanding

• Must be able to remain in a stationary position 50% of the time, with occasional movement in the office to access cabinets and equipment

• If you do not meet all the qualifications for this role, we still encourage you to apply, as we are always looking for diverse talent to join our growing team

What we offer:
A career that you define. Yes, we offer all the usual rewards and benefits - including medical, dental, vision, a wide variety of wellbeing offers, competitive salary, unlimited PTO, 401k with company match, paid volunteer days and more.

We provide an environment where new ideas are encouraged and celebrated, where people who want to have a real hand in our success thrive. We want people who want to make a difference - not just in the workplace, but in the industry and in the wider community.

What we’re looking for:

We are seeking a Salesforce-certified administrator and revenue operations expert to own and enhance the Salesforce experience for our Revenue team for 6 months. This role requires a strong blend of technical acumen, operational precision, and process improvement mindset. The ideal candidate is data-driven, detail-oriented, and passionate about enabling Sales team success through the seamless use of systems and tools.

  • 5+ years of experience in sales operations, revenue operations, or Salesforce program management

  • Deep expertise in Salesforce configuration, automation, and data integrity

  • Experience in book of business (BoB) management, account assignment strategies, and user permissions

  • Strong analytical skills with experience building custom dashboards, reports, and KPIs

  • Operational efficiency gains enabled by system/process improvements

As our Salesforce Revenue Program Manager, you’ll play a mission-critical role in empowering our Sales organization with the tools, data, and structure they need to thrive. You’ll ensure every account is in the right hands, every process is seamless, and every insight is actionable. By owning and optimizing our Salesforce platform, you’ll enable smarter selling, higher productivity, and a better customer experience, while driving revenue outcomes that matter.

jobs.title: Freelance Agent Evaluation Engineer
jobs.excerpt: Please submit your CV in English and indicate your level of English proficiency.
jobs.description:
Please submit your CV in English and indicate your level of English proficiency.

Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. Participation is project-based, not permanent employment.

We're building a dataset to evaluate AI coding agents - how well a model handles real-world developer tasks.

You'll create challenging tasks and evaluation criteria within realistic simulated environments:

  • Build realistic developer environments - a virtual company with codebase, infrastructure, and context (tickets, docs, conversations) that forms a believable development history
  • Design tasks from intermediate states of these environments - craft the prompt, define what "solved" means, and ensure the task is solvable by an AI agent
  • Write tests that verify agent solutions - accept all valid approaches and reject incorrect ones, neither too strict nor too lenient
  • Iterate on tasks and tests based on QA feedback - review agent solutions, analyze failures, and refine until the evaluation is fair and robust

What this is NOT:

  • Not data labeling
  • Not prompt engineering
  • Not writing code from scratch - the agent writes most of the code; you guide and evaluate

What we look for:

  • 5+ years in software development
  • Core stack: Python (FastAPI), JavaScript/TypeScript (React), Docker, Postgres, Kafka, Redis
  • Experience writing tests (functional, integration)
  • English proficiency - B2+

Why this is hard:
Frontier models are already good at coding. Creating a task that genuinely challenges the best models is non-trivial. You need to deeply understand where models fail and what scenarios reveal the difference between a good and a bad solution. Tasks have many valid solutions - writing tests that accept all correct solutions and reject incorrect ones is harder than it sounds.

Requirements and benefits

Educational qualifications

  • A Master’s Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science / Data Analytics, Artificial Intelligence / Machine Learning, Computational Linguistics / Natural Language Processing (NLP), Information Systems or other related fields.
  • Bachelor’s degree is accepted if only candidate has 5 years of experience in the field.

Academic and/or Professional Experience

Candidates should have a minimum of 3 years of professional experience in related roles or domain - specifically for QA-automation/testing or cybersecurity roles

How it works
Apply → Pass qualification(s) → Join a project → Complete tasks → Get paid

Compensation:
Paid per accepted task. Your rate depends on the qualification tier you reach and how efficiently you complete tasks — up to the equivalent of $40/hr. Because payment is per task, a faster pace raises your effective hourly rate.

Why this freelance opportunity might be a great fit for you?

  • Take part in a part-time, remote, freelance project that fits around your primary professional or academic commitments.
  • Work on advanced AI projects and gain valuable experience that enhances your portfolio. - Influence how future AI models understand and communicate in your field of expertise.

jobs.excerpt: Apply by 24th August 2026About Restless DevelopmentRestless Development Zambia is a youth-focused non-profit organisation that works with young people and communities to create lasting change.
jobs.description:
Apply by 24th August 2026

About Restless Development

Restless Development Zambia is a youth-focused non-profit organisation that works with young people and communities to create lasting change. We believe that young people are not only the leaders of tomorrow but also the leaders of today. By supporting young people to lead, influence and take action, we contribute to stronger communities and a more just, inclusive and equitable society.

Working in partnership with government, civil society, development partners and local communities, Restless Development Zambia delivers programmes across five strategic thematic areas: democracy, governance and civic participation; youth livelihoods and economic empowerment; gender and education; climate justice; and sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR).

Restless Development Zambia is governed by an independent National Board, which provides strategic leadership, oversight and accountability, ensuring that the organisation remains focused on its mission, delivers high-quality programmes, and upholds the highest standards of governance.

We are part of the wider Restless Development global network, comprising independently registered and governed hubs in India, Nepal, Sierra Leone, Tanzania, Uganda, the United Kingdom, the United States, Zambia and Zimbabwe. Together with the Youth Collective—a growing global community of youth-led organisations with members in over 185 countries—we support the collective power of young people to create a better world.

At Restless Development, we are committed to shifting power to young people by ensuring they have meaningful opportunities to influence decisions and lead change within their communities, nationally, and globally.

Our Approach to Safeguarding

Restless Development Zambia is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and adults at risk. The safety, dignity and wellbeing of the people and communities we work with are paramount and take precedence over the delivery of programmes or the achievement of organisational objectives.

Safeguarding is everyone's responsibility. We expect all Board members, staff, volunteers and partners to uphold the highest standards of conduct, comply with our Safeguarding Policy, and contribute to creating a safe and inclusive environment free from abuse, exploitation and harm.

About Our Zambia National Board

The Restless Development Zambia National Board is the governing body of the organisation, providing strategic leadership, oversight and accountability. The Board ensures that the organisation remains focused on its mission, is financially sustainable, operates with integrity, and delivers meaningful impact for young people and communities across Zambia.

Board Members serve in a voluntary capacity and ordinarily meet on a quarterly basis, with additional meetings convened where necessary. The Board works closely with the Hub Director and Leadership Team, providing strategic guidance and governance oversight while supporting the effective leadership and long-term sustainability of the organisation. The Zambia National Board is responsible for:

  • Providing strategic leadership by guiding the organisation's strategic direction and supporting the implementation of its strategy and priorities in Zambia.
  • Providing governance oversight by supporting the appointment of the Hub Director, overseeing organisational performance, and ensuring that the organisation operates in line with its values, policies and statutory obligations.
  • Providing financial oversight by reviewing and monitoring the organisation's annual budgets, financial performance, statutory compliance and audited financial statements.
  • Strengthening partnerships and organisational profile by using members' professional networks to support strategic engagement with government, development partners, the private sector and other key stakeholders.
  • Supporting resource mobilisation by opening doors to funding opportunities, providing strategic advice on resource mobilisation, and promoting the long-term sustainability of the organisation

Time Commitment

Board Members serve on a voluntary basis and are expected to make an active contribution to the governance and strategic direction of Restless Development Zambia. The expected commitment includes:

  • Attending four quarterly Board meetings each year and the Annual Board Away Day, together with any additional meetings convened where necessary.
  • Serving on one of the Board's standing sub-committees, including Programmes and Operations, People, Safeguarding and Governance, or Risk and Audit, and participating in meetings as required.
  • Providing strategic guidance and oversight to the Hub Director and Leadership Team between Board meetings, where appropriate.
  • Supporting the organisation's resource mobilisation efforts by identifying opportunities, making strategic introductions, and promoting the work of Restless Development Zambia.
  • Acting as an ambassador for Restless Development Zambia by upholding the organisation's values and strengthening its profile through personal and professional networks.
  • Representing the organisation at selected meetings, events and stakeholder engagements, where appropriate.
  • Board Members are expected to dedicate sufficient time to prepare for meetings, review Board papers in advance, and actively contribute to discussions and decision-making.

Personal Specification

We are seeking individuals who are committed to good governance and share Restless Development Zambia's vision of creating opportunities for young people to lead change in their communities.

As a Board Member, you will bring strategic thinking, sound judgement, integrity and a willingness to contribute your time, knowledge and experience to support the organisation's long-term success. You will demonstrate the personal qualities that reflect Restless Development's values and be committed to promoting accountability, transparency and ethical leadership.

Applicants should have strong professional experience and a good understanding of the Zambian development landscape. We are particularly interested in individuals who can contribute strategic insight, strengthen the Board's governance role, and help expand the organisation's relationships and influence across government, civil society, development partners, academia, the private sector, youth networks and other key stakeholders.

We are particularly interested in candidates with expertise in one or more of the following areas:

  • Risk Management and Audit
  • Finance and Accounting
  • Legal and Corporate Governance
  • Resource Mobilisation and Strategy

How to Apply

We particularly encourage applications from individuals with experience serving on governing boards, audit committees, finance committees, or senior leadership teams within the public, private or non-profit sectors.

Interested candidates are invited to submit:

  • A current Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Résumé; and
  • A brief cover letter (maximum two pages) outlining your interest in joining the Restless Development Zambia National Board and how your skills, experience and expertise would contribute to the organisation's governance and strategic direction. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Before applying, applicants are encouraged to review the Board Member Job Description to gain a clear understanding of the role, responsibilities, and expectations.

Click here to view the Board Member Job Description.

Equal Opportunities

Restless Development Zambia is an Equal Opportunities Organisation and welcomes applications from individuals of all backgrounds. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive Board that reflects the communities we serve. Selection will be based on merit. We do not discriminate on the basis of gender, age, disability, marital status, race, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, HIV status, or any other characteristic unrelated to the requirements of the role.

Salary: This is a voluntary role, and is not remunerated.

You will translate Finance and business problems into structured analytical frameworks, scalable data products, and practical AI-enabled solutions that improve decision quality and operational efficiency.

The ideal candidate can connect business context to strong execution: partnering with stakeholders to clarify business problems, while also being hands-on enough to query data, prototype solutions, pressure-test metrics, and partner with technical teams to support scalable solutions. This is an individual contributor role that requires strong business judgment, technical depth, product thinking, and the ability to influence across teams.

Responsibilities

  • Own analytics and AI-enabled workflow workstreams, from problem framing and stakeholder alignment to solution design, insight generation, adoption, and measurable business impact

  • Analyze business and financial metrics to uncover key drivers of growth, retention, churn, productivity, and efficiency, and recommend clear data-backed actions

  • Contribute to scalable, repeatable analytics frameworks and best practices that improve Finance decision-making and create consistency across planning, forecasting, reporting, and business reviews

  • Apply strong governance, quality control, and documentation practices to ensure AI-enabled workflows are accurate, explainable, secure, and appropriate for Finance decision support

  • Communicate insights, recommendations, and roadmap tradeoffs to stakeholders and leadership through clear storytelling, executive-ready presentations, and concise written narratives

jobs.title: Spring 2027 Legal Internship (US)
jobs.excerpt: The Center for International Environmental Law (CIEL) is a dynamic, nonprofit organization that works at the intersection of human rights and the environment.
jobs.description:
The Center for International Environmental Law (CIEL) is a dynamic, nonprofit organization that works at the intersection of human rights and the environment. CIEL is comprised of attorneys, campaigners, researchers, and communicators who have extensive experience in leading international strategies to advance everyone’s right to a healthy environment. Many of our program areas explore innovative developments in international environmental law and human rights, including in their direct link with other international legal fields, such as international investment law or international trade law.

Our legal internship program offers a unique opportunity for law students to develop skills in the field of international environmental law, and using legal strategies to protect human rights and the environment. Learning from and supervised by a diverse staff of experts and attorneys, internships offer insight into innovative developments in international environmental law and human rights, by honing thoughtful and creative research and analysis. Offering this internship is central to CIEL’s mission of developing the next generation of environmental leaders and lawyers through real-world training and practice.

Responsibilities of a legal intern may include researching and writing about areas of domestic and international law, including environmental and human rights law, international investment law, and international trade law and policy; assisting with policy analysis and advocacy; attending meetings and conferences; assisting with the production of CIEL publications, legal opinions and legal briefs; support in the preparation of amicus curiae before international tribunals and otherwise working closely with CIEL staff on various projects. Successful applicants generally possess excellent research and writing skills and a strong dedication to public interest law.

Stipend:

A monthly stipend is available for any intern eligible to receive it under the rules applied by their jurisdiction and educational institution. The basic stipend is $2,600 per month for a full-time internship in Washington, DC. For less than full-time internships, the stipend is prorated according to the intern’s approximate level of time commitment to CIEL. Stipends are intended to make the CIEL internship more readily available to aspiring professionals, and are not intended to provide compensation, create a legal or employment relationship between the intern and CIEL, or otherwise modify the legal nature of the internship program.

Requirements:

  • Applicants should be enrolled in a course of study leading to a postgraduate law degree (JD, LLM) or similar professional qualification for the duration of the internship. We cannot accept recent graduates.
  • Applicants must possess some experience with international environmental or human rights law, either through graduate-level courses or work experience.
  • Applicants must be willing to make a ten-week commitment of 15 hours/week.

To Apply:

  • To apply, please submit your cover letter, resume, and a writing sample (please, no legal memos - see FAQ below for more information). Please not send transcripts.

Application Deadline:

  • Spring 2027 US Internship Application Deadline: Friday, November 20, 2026.

    FAQ:
  • May I undertake my internship remotely? All CIEL legal internships may be carried out remotely. Please note that we can only consider applicants for this US internship who will carry out their internship while physically residing in the United States. Remote work from other countries cannot be accommodated.
  • What time period does the spring session cover? Roughly January through May, although we can be flexible regarding starting and ending dates.
  • What should I submit as a writing sample? Feel free to submit something that you feel demonstrates your writing ability. This can include undergraduate work. Please avoid 1L legal writing memos if possible.
  • May I apply to both offices? You may apply to both our Geneva and Washington, DC offices. Applying for internships with our Geneva office is a separate process, please see that application page.
  • Will CIEL sponsor a visa for me?CIEL in the United States is unable to sponsor visas. For non-US citizens, you must be a currently enrolled student in the US and would undertake your internship as part of your university-sponsored student visa.
  • Does CIEL offer internships to college students? We're sorry, but due to the nature of our work CIEL cannot offer undergraduate internships at this time.

If you have further questions or need assistance, please contact .
