jobs.description:
Job Title: QA / Test Automation EngineerJob Category: EngineeringTime Type: Full timeMinimum Clearance Required to Start: Public TrustEmployee Type: RegularPercentage of Travel Required: Up to 10%Type of Travel: Local* * *

The Opportunity:
CACI is seeking a Mid-Level QA / Test Automation Engineer to support an agile software modernization program by planning, executing, and documenting manual and automated testing of Java-based applications hosted in Amazon Web Services (AWS). Working with moderate independence, this role validates application functionality, APIs, integrations, databases, data exchanges, and legacy-system interfaces; develops and maintains automated regression tests using industry-standard test automation tools; and collaborates with cross-functional teams to confirm that releases meet business, technical, security, accessibility, and operational requirements.

Responsibilities:
In this role, the candidate will have practical experience testing Java applications in AWS and hands-on experience using automated testing tools to support a large-scale Grant Solutions platform modernization effort. The tester will independently complete assigned testing activities, identify and communicate quality risks, and help ensure that cloud-hosted capabilities are reliable, secure, accessible, data-consistent, and ready for release.

The tester will translate user stories and acceptance criteria into test scenarios; execute end-to-end, integration, API, database, and regression testing across AWS environments; log and retest defects; prepare test data and evidence; and build reusable automated tests for stable, repeatable scenarios. The role contributes to—but is not expected to architect—the program’s automation framework, AWS-based CI/CD quality gates, test processes, and release-readiness reporting.

  • Review user stories, acceptance criteria, Java application designs, API specifications, data mappings, and AWS environment documentation to identify test conditions and expected results.

  • Create, execute, and maintain manual test cases for functional, system, regression, smoke, integration, API, database, data validation, and user acceptance testing.

  • Develop, enhance, and maintain automated test scripts, reusable components, test data, locators, and regression suites using appropriate automated testing tools.

  • Use automated testing tools to test web user interfaces, REST or SOAP APIs, databases, and end-to-end business processes, as applicable.

  • Execute automated tests across AWS-hosted test environments; analyze results, logs, screenshots, and execution evidence; troubleshoot failures; and maintain tests as the Java applications evolve.

  • Test Java-based application components and their interactions with AWS services, APIs, databases, authentication services, data exchanges, legacy systems, workflows, reports, and downstream systems.

  • Validate application behavior across AWS environments and use available application, cloud, and pipeline logs to support defect isolation and root-cause analysis.

  • Prepare and manage test data, capture test evidence, maintain requirements traceability, and document testing outcomes.

  • Log defects with clear reproduction steps, expected and actual results, severity, AWS environment details, and supporting evidence; participate in defect triage and verify fixes.

  • Collaborate with Java developers, Product Owners, Scrum Masters, AWS and DevSecOps engineers, integration and data teams, security specialists, vendors, and business stakeholders throughout the sprint and release lifecycle.

  • Support automated test execution in CI/CD pipelines, scheduled regression runs, and release validation; investigate failures and improve test reliability with senior QA and DevSecOps staff.

  • Contribute to test estimates, sprint planning, test coverage reviews, release-readiness assessments, quality metrics, and continuous improvement of AWS and automated testing practices.

Qualifications:

Required:

  • Must be able to obtain and maintain a Federal Public Trust; candidates must receive approved adjudication before onboarding. Candidates with an active Public Trust or suitability determination are preferred.

  • Bachelor’s degree required.

  • Four (4) years of experience in software quality assurance, application testing, system testing, or a related technical role.

  • Hands-on experience testing Java-based web applications, services, APIs, integrations, and data flows.

jobs.description:
Worth AI is hiring a Senior Agentic AI Engineer to design and ship production agent systems that automate KYB, underwriting, and risk decisions on regulated financial data. You’ll own agents end-to-end architecture, retrieval, tools, evals, and production deployment and partner closely with our Chief AI Officer, applied scientists, and platform teams.

Responsibilities

  • Design and ship multi-step agentic systems (planner/executor, tool-using, multi-agent, human-in-the-loop) for onboarding, underwriting, case review, and continuous monitoring.
  • Architect agent graphs in LangGraph (or comparable — CrewAI, AutoGen, Claude Agent SDK) with explicit state, durable execution, retries, and safe fallbacks.
  • Build the retrieval layer powering our agents — chunking, hybrid search, reranking, and grounded citation.
  • Own the eval stack: golden sets, offline regression suites, LLM-as-judge, online A/B and shadow evals, and red-teaming for jailbreaks, prompt injection, and PII leakage.
  • Expose agents to production systems via well-typed tools and MCP servers. Treat tool surface area as a product.
  • Drive production MLOps: deployment, versioning, traffic shaping, cost/latency budgets, tracing, and on-call playbooks for agent incidents.
  • Partner with security and compliance to keep agents inside SOC 2, GDPR, CCPA, and fair-lending posture — auditability and explainability built in, not bolted on.
  • Mentor engineers on agent patterns, prompt hygiene, eval discipline, and LLM failure modes.
  • Technology Stack
    • Languages: Python, Node.js, TypeScript
    • Agent / LLM frameworks: LangGraph, LangChain, Claude Agent SDK, MCP, OpenAI SDK
    • Models: Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, open-weight where appropriate
    • Retrieval & Data: PostgreSQL, pgvector, OpenSearch, Kafka, Redshift, Redis
    • Infra: AWS, Kubernetes (EKS), ArgoCD, Terraform
    • Evals & Observability: LangSmith / Langfuse / Braintrust-style tooling, DataDog

Requirements

  • 5+ years of software engineering experience, with 2+ years building production LLM or agentic systems (not just notebooks or demos).
  • Hands-on experience with a modern agent framework (LangGraph strongly preferred) and a track record of shipping agents that run, fail gracefully, and recover.
  • Strong RAG fundamentals chunking, embeddings, hybrid retrieval, reranking, grounding — and judgment about when RAG isn’t the right answer.
  • Real eval experience golden sets, offline and online evaluations, used to make ship/no-ship calls.
  • Production MLOps fluency: deployed LLM workloads under real latency, cost, and reliability constraints.
  • Strong Python; comfortable in TypeScript / Node.js.
  • Solid systems engineering instincts APIs, async patterns, queues, databases, distributed system failure modes.
  • Calibrated communicator; thrives in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
  • Prior experience in fintech, lending, payments, KYB/KYC, fraud, or AML.
  • Experience building MCP servers or other structured tool interfaces for LLMs.
  • Background in classical ML (ranking, scoring, calibration).
  • Experience designing explainable / auditable AI workflows for regulated environments.
  • Open-source contributions to agent frameworks, eval tooling, or retrieval libraries.
  • AWS depth (EKS, MSK, RDS, S3, Lambda) and IaC with Terraform.

Success Metrics

  • Agent Quality: Measurable improvements in task success rate, grounding accuracy, and hallucination rate on our eval suites.
  • Production Reliability: Agents you own meet defined SLOs for latency (P90/P99), tool-call success, and cost per task.
  • Velocity: New agent capabilities go from prototype to production in weeks, without skipping evals or guardrails.
  • Risk Posture: Zero material incidents tied to prompt injection, PII leakage, or unsafe tool use on agents you own.
  • Force Multiplier: Patterns, tools, and eval scaffolding you build get adopted across engineering.

jobs.excerpt: About the role: We run a distributed, camera-based video monitoring and AI alerting platform.
jobs.description:
About the role:

We run a distributed, camera-based video monitoring and AI alerting platform. The system spans the full spectrum of modern and legacy infrastructure: an AWS-hosted fleet of Java microservices and workers, a GPU-backed computer-vision inference pipeline, a real-time streaming and presence layer, and thousands of on-premise edge "media boxes" deployed in the field that ingest camera feeds, serve HLS video, and stream events back to the cloud.

This is a reliability-first role. Your primary job is to keep a large, mixed operational estate healthy at scale: meaningful service objectives, trustworthy alerting, sound capacity, tested disaster recovery, and fast, calm incident response. Delivery pipelines matter, but here they exist in service of reliability, not the other way around. We are not hiring a pipeline-and-self-service DevOps engineer who treats operations as a side concern. We are hiring an SRE who owns uptime and operational quality, and who can write the software to make that uptime measurable and automatic.

If you think in SLOs, error budgets, and blameless postmortems, and you are happiest when a noisy, fragile system becomes quiet and predictable on your watch, this is your role.

What you'll keep reliableYou will own the operational health of all of the following:
  • Computer-vision / AI models: frame-based inference services running on GPU EC2 (g4dn-class, AWS Deep Learning AMIs), fed by camera frames from S3 and a Kafka (Amazon MSK) event bus, with Redis (ElastiCache) for state. Outputs flow through an alerts pipeline (OutgoingInferenceMessage to SNS/IoT to notification workers).
  • Python services: the AI/alerts inference tier and supporting tooling.
  • Legacy Java services: ~140 Java 8 services and libraries (REST APIs, SQS/SNS workers, Lambda functions) running on Jetty 9.4, deployed to Elastic Beanstalk, ECS, and Lambda.
  • Edge appliances ("media boxes"): Ubuntu 22.04 / Docker Compose appliances managed remotely over AWS IoT Core secure tunnelling, with Cloudflare tunnels for egress. Includes an active CentOS 7 to containerized-stack migration effort.
  • Data and messaging backbone: PostgreSQL (RDS) across many schemas, TimescaleDB for analytics, Redis, DynamoDB, Amazon MSK (Kafka), SQS/SNS, and Kinesis.

What you'll do Reliability and operations (the core of the role)
  • Own service objectives. Define SLIs and SLOs for the services that matter, manage error budgets, and use them to drive prioritization and change-rate decisions. Make reliability a measured number, not a feeling.
  • Make observability trustworthy. Own alert quality end-to-end: high signal-to-noise, alarms that reliably catch the incidents they are meant to catch, and the discipline to turn off a misleading alarm until it is fixed properly. Build the dashboards and the custom metrics, exporters, and instrumentation (CloudWatch, OpenTelemetry) needed to see the system clearly.
  • Lead incident response. Run incidents calmly, drive mean-time-to-recovery down, and produce blameless postmortems with action items that actually get closed. Improve and own the on-call rotation and its health.
  • Plan capacity and performance. Forecast and right-size compute (especially GPU), Kafka/MSK throughput and partitioning, RDS/TimescaleDB load, and Redis. Catch saturation before customers do.
  • Own business continuity and disaster recovery. Backups, replication, failover, and recovery for RDS, MSK, Redis, and the edge fleet. Define RPO/RTO and prove them with regular, tested game days, not assumptions.
  • Keep the edge fleet healthy. Remote diagnosis and recovery over AWS IoT, container auto-update over systemd timers, and the ongoing CentOS 7 migration to the containerized media stack (Ubuntu 22.04).
  • Engineer away toil. Write real software (Python, Golang, Bash) to automate operational work, self-heal common failures, and make reliability repeatable instead of heroic.
  • Govern production change safely. Enforce collaborative, reviewed change management; protect the system from risky, unilateral changes (topology, instance-count, scaling, and config).

Delivery and platform (in support of reliability)
  • Keep CI/CD healthy and safe: CircleCI with Bazel/Gradle builds, OIDC-based AWS auth, container builds to ECR, and EB/ECS/Lambda deploys, tuned so that releases are safe, observable, and reversible.
  • Maintain Terraform for the AWS estate (compute, networking, IAM, databases, messaging, monitoring), following our module-based conventions and S3-backed state.
  • Harden security and compliance: IAM least-privilege, Secrets Manager/KMS, TLS and certificate management (including IoT device certificates), CloudTrail, and AWS Config.


Requirements


  • AWS certification is mandatory. A current AWS Certified DevOps Engineer – Professional or AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional is strongly preferred.
  • 10+ years in Site Reliability Engineering or production operations at scale. We do not expect mastery of every area below on day one. We expect real depth in several and the ability to ramp quickly on the rest.
  • Demonstrated SLO/error-budget practice. You have defined SLIs and SLOs, run against an error budget, and used it to make real decisions.
  • Strong production observability skills. Deep with metrics, logs, alarming, and dashboards (CloudWatch, OpenTelemetry, and/or Prometheus/Grafana/Datadog), and able to build the instrumentation when it does not exist.
  • Proven incident command. You have led incidents, owned an on-call rotation, and written postmortems that changed how a system behaved.
  • Capacity planning and performance experience across compute, databases, and a messaging or streaming system (Kafka/MSK ideal).
  • Disaster recovery ownership: backups, replication, failover, and tested RPO/RTO.
  • Software engineering ability for automation. Comfortable writing Python, Golang, and Bash to build reliability tooling, not just configure off-the-shelf tools.
  • Expert with Terraform (or equivalent IaC) and strong Linux administration (shell plus Linux GNU utils), comfortable from cloud to bare-metal/edge.
  • Database operations experience with PostgreSQL (time-series a plus).
  • A reliability mindset: you instrument before you guess, and you write the runbook.
Nice to have
  • Operating GPU workloads and serving computer-vision or ML models in production (CUDA, Deep Learning AMIs, inference scaling).
  • Apache MSK / Kafka and streaming-data operations (Kinesis, Kinesis Video Streams).
  • AWS IoT Core at scale: device provisioning, certificates, secure tunnelling.
  • Managing a fleet of edge / on-premise devices (golden images, remote update, systemd).
  • Operating and modernizing legacy systems (Java 8, Jetty, CentOS).
  • Chaos engineering / game-day practice, and capacity modeling.
  • Familiarity with Bazel in a monorepo; Cloudflare, Cognito/Auth0, API Gateway.

How we work, and what we expect from this hire:

These principles reflect lessons we take seriously. The right candidate already operates this way:
  • Observability must be trustworthy. Alarms that cry wolf are worse than no alarms. You own alert quality end-to-end: high signal-to-noise, alarms that reliably catch the incidents they are meant to catch, and the judgment to turn off a misleading alarm until it is fixed properly rather than leave a noisy one firing. We have felt the cost of unreliable alerting and want someone who closes that gap and keeps it closed.
  • Change management is collaborative, never unilateral. Any infrastructure change that affects a service is made together with the engineer who owns and understands that service. Scaling, instance-count, topology, and config changes are reviewed with that owner before they ship. Single-instance vs. multi-instance assumptions, in particular, are never changed on a guess.
  • Follow-through over activity. We measure outcomes, not effort or hours. When something is asked for, we expect it driven to a correct, durable resolution on a reasonable timeline, not left half-solved for months. Find what is actually needed, focus on it, and finish it.
  • Prefer the right fix to a quick patch. Solve the root cause. Do not paper over it and move on.

jobs.excerpt: About IrthIrth is building Sentinel, a unified data and analytics platform that evolves our Asset Integrity for Pipelines product from a point risk-scoring feature into a comprehensive threat-management platform.
jobs.description:
About Irth

Irth is building Sentinel, a unified data and analytics platform that evolves our Asset Integrity for Pipelines product from a point risk-scoring feature into a comprehensive threat-management platform.

Sentinel connects asset integrity, damage prevention, stakeholder management, and land management. The platform will support industry-standard, Irth-built, and customer-built ("bring your own model") risk models across both transmission and distribution integrity management programs.

We are hiring a Technical Product Manager dedicated full-time to Sentinel. This is a hands-on product role at the intersection of data engineering, applied analytics, and regulated workflow software.

You will own product requirements and delivery across a multi-phase roadmap that includes:

  • Building a unified data platform with AI-driven ETL
  • Decoupling risk models into a standalone analytical layer
  • Launching a model governance and BYOM (Bring Your Own Model) framework
  • Expanding Sentinel from transmission into distribution use cases

The Product Challenge

The defining challenge of Sentinel is not the models — it is the data.

The industry risk models we support require approximately 65 input attributes. Our products natively cover most, but not all, of these attributes, while customer data arrives in many forms, including spreadsheets, PDFs, inspection reports, and field notes.

Your core product challenge will be closing that data gap through automated ingestion, normalization, quality repair, and reconciliation, rather than relying on services-heavy customer onboarding.

We are open on level. Title and scope will be calibrated to the experience you bring. Strong candidates at both the mid- and senior-level individual contributor range are encouraged to apply.

What You'll Do

Own Product Definition

  • Translate a phased product strategy and high-level requirements into a groomed, traceable backlog of epics, features, user stories, and acceptance criteria that engineering can execute against without ambiguity.
  • Drive discovery with design partners and prospective customers, translating operational and regulatory realities into clear product requirements.
  • Maintain the roadmap against defined phase gates and hold the team accountable to delivery criteria, including:
    • Data platform operational
    • Data lineage traceable
    • Risk models decoupled
    • BYOM framework live
    • Distribution capabilities generally available

Lead the Data & Analytics Workstream

  • Partner with data architects, data engineers, and data scientists to define the unified data platform, ingestion and normalization layer, and data-quality capabilities.
  • Define requirements for automated data-quality repair, drift monitoring, and reconciliation.
  • Specify connectors to customer systems of record and external data providers, including weather, soil, satellite imagery, and locate-ticket sources.
  • Define entity-resolution requirements and shared spatial data capabilities so records can be reconciled to common assets across product lines.
  • Own requirements for model configuration, versioning, governance, and audit trails across industry, Irth, and customer-built models.

Make Agentic AI a Delivery Advantage

  • Shape agentic AI workflows for document parsing and schema mapping.
  • Scope proofs of concept and define human-in-the-loop review thresholds and quality standards for production deployment.
  • Use AI tooling as part of your own product development workflow. Irth uses Claude Code for agentic software development, and we expect Product to work alongside Engineering in that environment rather than simply handing requirements over the wall.

Deliver in a Regulated Environment

  • Translate federal pipeline safety regulations into executable product logic, auditable outputs, and defensible reporting.
  • Define requirements for traceability, compliance documentation, and outputs suitable for utility rate-case filings.
  • Define validation and sensitivity-testing requirements for every model release before commercial launch.
  • Partner with Engineering and Security to establish the non-functional product bar, including:
    • Multi-tenant isolation
    • Access control
    • Calculation reproducibility
    • Auditability
    • Security-attestation readiness

Run the Delivery Cadence

  • Drive agile execution across a cross-functional team, including sprint planning, dependency management, release discipline, and delivery metrics.
  • Coordinate across data, application, GIS, and QA workstreams and proactively resolve cross-team dependencies.
  • Partner with Product Marketing, Sales Engineering, and Account teams on design-partner enablement, pilot feedback loops, and launch readiness.

What Success Looks Like

You will help Sentinel move from a point risk-scoring capability to a scalable threat-management platform that can:

  • Reliably ingest and normalize complex customer data
  • Reduce manual, services-heavy onboarding
  • Provide traceable and trusted data lineage
  • Support multiple risk-model frameworks
  • Enable customers to bring and govern their own models
  • Deliver auditable, reproducible analytical results
  • Expand from transmission into distribution integrity management
  • Use AI to materially improve data onboarding and product delivery

Requirements

What You'll Bring

Required Qualifications

  • 4+ years of experience in technical product management, product ownership, or a closely related role delivering enterprise software, ideally where data quality, analytics, or modeling was central to the product's value proposition.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate data science and statistical modeling concepts into governed, structured, and actionable end-user workflows, and to communicate model behavior effectively to non-technical stakeholders.
  • Hands-on fluency with data, including schema design and alignment, pipeline and ingestion design, handling missing or inconsistent data, and governance practices that make outputs defensible and audit-ready.
  • Practical experience applying AI to product and delivery workflows, including prompt engineering, AI-assisted workflow automation, or agent design, with sound judgment about where AI belongs in a workflow and where it does not.
  • Track record of delivering products in regulated or compliance-driven environments and translating external requirements into working software against fixed deadlines.
  • Experience with complex integrations, data migrations, or platform transformations, particularly customer migrations from legacy systems to modern platforms.
  • Strong agile delivery skills and the credibility to run a technical team's delivery cadence, including backlog health, capacity planning, dependency management, and consistent on-time releases.
  • Working familiarity with our technology stack, or the demonstrated ability to ramp quickly: Databricks, Azure, GitHub, Atlassian (Jira/Confluence), and AI coding tools.
  • Excellent written communication skills. Much of this role involves producing requirements, specifications, and decision documents that must withstand engineering and regulatory scrutiny.
  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering, analytics, or a related technical field.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in pipeline integrity management, oil and gas, utilities, or another asset-heavy industrial domain. This is genuinely preferred, but not required. We will invest in bringing the right product leader up to speed on the domain, supported by subject-matter experts across the team.
  • Familiarity with federal pipeline safety regulations, integrity management programs, or comparable safety-critical regulatory frameworks.
  • Working knowledge of GIS and geospatial data.
  • Hands-on analytics or programming experience with Python, R, or SQL, sufficient to independently interrogate datasets rather than waiting on a data queue.
  • Experience with BI and data visualization tools for translating model outputs into executive-ready reporting.
  • Advanced degree in analytics, data science, or a related field.
  • Agile or project management certification such as CSM, CAPM, PMP, or similar.

Location & Travel

This is a fully remote role open to candidates based anywhere in the United States.

Occasional travel is required for team working sessions, on-site meetings with design partners, and meetings with prospective customers.

Why Join Sentinel

  • Executive-backed strategic program: Sentinel is a named strategic initiative with executive sponsorship, a funded multi-year roadmap, and design-partner traction with major operators already underway.
  • Own the platform end to end: You will own a platform from the data layer up — not just a slice of an existing product. You will have meaningful influence over architecture, product sequencing, and how AI is applied across the platform.
  • Work that makes a difference: Better risk data and better models help pipeline operators identify threats before they become incidents. The work directly contributes to safer, more reliable delivery of the natural gas that powers our society, economy, and way of life.

AI Use in Hiring

As part of our hiring process, this role may use artificial intelligence (AI) or automated tools to assist with reviewing and screening applications. These tools support, but do not replace, human judgment in hiring decisions.

Role Type

This is a New position.

Compensation

The salary range for this role is USD $150K

This range reflects base salary only and does not include other compensation components. Offers are determined based on several factors, including, but not limited to, experience, skills, qualifications, and location.

Benefits

What We Offer

  • Join a dynamic, growing company with a strong reputation in its industry.
  • Competitive salary.
  • Comprehensive health plan options, including medical, dental, and vision coverage.
  • 401(k) plan with company match.
  • Flexible PTO policy plus company-paid holidays.
  • Additional benefits, including life insurance, pet insurance, and employee discounts and perks programs.
  • Generous one-time work-from-home stipend to help you set up your home workspace.
  • Company events and opportunities to connect, including monthly team lunches, volunteer outings, and quarterly gatherings.
  • Hybrid employees have access to complimentary snacks, beverages, and coffee at our Columbus, Ohio office.

About Us

This isn't incremental work – it's the kind of experience that changes the trajectory of a career.

We believe in the power of positive human experiences, and that a deep sense of belonging creates cohesion in our culture. Even as a remote-first team, you'll be a contributor and custodian of that culture, solving complex problems alongside talented people who are just as driven to help us deliver on our brand promise and build 'a better way to pay' at Zepto.

About the Role

As a Senior Security Engineer (Product Security), you will play a significant role in keeping our product safe and secure by building on and maturing Zepto's product security practices. You will work hands-on and shoulder-to-shoulder with Engineering and Product teams, providing guidance and coaching across the software development life cycle while continuing to raise the bar on our security expectations and capability.

This is a security role at its core, but not a gatekeeping one. We are builders – we expect you to read and write production-level code, build tooling and automation, and contribute paved-road solutions that engineers actually want to use.

Reporting to the Security Engineering Lead, you will work closely with them to develop and build Zepto's product security strategy and approach. You will apply a consultative and advisory approach when working with the wider Zepto team, empowering them to work confidently and to use the self-service capabilities you help establish.

We have excellent working relationships with our developers and we need to keep it that way. We are not the team of no. We are the team that helps make things better.

Zepto is moving quickly towards an AI-native way of building and operating. You will be someone who is already experimenting with AI and agentic tooling, or is genuinely keen to, and who is open to developing the skills to secure these systems as we adopt them.

Within the Security team, you are the go-to person for:

  • Secure development practices
  • Vulnerability management
  • Security architecture advice

Working in a scale-up, means you get the opportunity to flex your skills in a variety of ways. We are agile and always willing to roll up our sleeves to get things done. You can, however, expect your day to day to be involved in the following:

  • Coach engineering teams and collaborate to ensure every step of the software development life cycle follows security best practices
  • Design, build and maintain security tooling, automation and paved-road controls as production-quality software
  • Conduct security assessments and architecture reviews of Zepto's applications and services
  • Embed within project teams to ensure they are effectively considering information security risk and prioritising security controls
  • Establish and document security architecture and practices in collaboration with the Security Engineering Lead, Product and Engineering teams
  • Work with the Security Engineering Lead to support Zepto's adoption of AI and agentic systems, and experiment with AI tooling to improve how the Security team works
  • Help manage application security incidents in collaboration with the rest of the Security team

About You

You’re a generalist Security Engineer with diverse experience that knows how to get things done. You have proven knowledge of security best practices and how to implement them in a scale-up environment.

Specifically, we’d welcome any candidate who has the following experience:

  • The ability to read and write production code and build tooling and automation, with a software engineering foundation (Go and/or Python preferred, but engineers in any language will be considered)
  • Experience implementing and maintaining common application security tooling
  • Hands-on experience automating security controls
  • Experience working in cloud infrastructure (AWS)
  • Proven experience advising engineering teams on security architecture best practices
  • Actively experimenting with, or a demonstrated appetite to experiment with, AI and agentic technologies, and an interest in securing them
  • A strong and empathic communicator with both technical and non-technical teams

While Zepto is a remote-first organisation with a national footprint, our preference is for this role to be based in Melbourne, Sydney or Brisbane. We’re looking for Zeptonians who hold long-term, permanent status in Australia—specifically Australian Citizens or Permanent Residents. While we’d love to welcome everyone, we aren't equipped to offer visa sponsorship or consider temporary work visas for this role right now.

Regardless of where you are located in Australia, you’ll enjoy the flexibility of our remote-first model and be supported by great leadership to learn and grow, with the added benefit of our co-working hubs for those who value a hybrid environment or for that social connection.

Why Zepto?

Headquartered in beautiful Byron Bay, Zepto has an inspiring founder story and is a customer-focused, culture-first organisation. You’ll be joining a team that champions curiosity and a pioneering perspective, and thrives in a fast-moving sector.

Just some of Zepto’s commitments to it’s people include:

  • Join a Talented Team: Work with world-class talent and leaders who support career growth
  • Flexible Work: A remote-first work culture, with the opportunity to work anywhere in Australia. You’ll also get access to premium co-working spaces and a Byron, Sydney & Melbourne Hub
  • Paid Parental Leave: 12 weeks Paid Parental Leave for primary caregivers and 4 weeks for secondary caregivers
  • Wellbeing Focus: Access to Zepto’s Wellbeing Menu, which includes 3 x paid Wellbeing Days per year and access to an Employee Assistance Program
  • Annual Learning Budget: An individual learning budget, and 4 x paid Growth & Impact Days annually to focus on professional development
  • Remote-Work Support: A $500 Remote Work Budget to set up your home office upon commencement, and $300 annually from your 2nd Zeptoversary
